about: What a value is allowed to be, and what a consumer must do with one it cannot hold. Every case here came out of running a real library through an exporter and finding something the format had no way to say.

cases.why: One task belongs to two projects; one note cites four sources. A reference that can only be scalar makes the commonest shape in a knowledge base unsayable, and a producer meeting that wall will either drop the extras or smuggle them into a field nobody can read. `many` declares it, and a declared cardinality is checkable: a many field holds a list, a single field does not.

The check has to bite both ways or it is not a declaration, it is a hint. A producer that stores every reference as a one-element array and declares none of them `many` has told consumers nothing, and the first tool to read a value rather than a list will show an id where a name should be.

A tool whose model allows one project per task may take the first and carry on — refusing the import helps nobody — but the user has just silently lost a relationship they made deliberately. Taking the first quietly is the same failure as importing completion-anchored recurrence as schedule-anchored: it looks right and it is wrong, and only the report gives anyone a chance to notice.

Real libraries are full of empty strings where a field was opened and left alone, and the format said both ends of a span were optional without ever saying what "" meant. One consumer reads it as no start; another reads a start that fails to parse and shows the epoch, or today, or nothing with no explanation. It is absent. Producers should omit it and consumers must treat it as omitted.

The list of value kinds is open. A producer with a kind the format has never heard of declares it anyway and it travels untouched — the alternative is that the field's type becomes unsayable and only its values survive, which leaves a consumer holding data it cannot describe. Consumers treat an unknown kind as opaque: carry it, do not coerce it, do not drop the field.

A document with a body and some metadata about it is the dominant shape in this genre — a Markdown file with frontmatter is exactly that — and a format where everything must be a property has nowhere to put the body. `content` is the one reserved slot outside the bag, and a profile may name it as the body. Producers that keep the body in a field carry on doing so; nothing changes for them.
